title: A design can be SKIPPED: the aggregate records the skip and the decoder refuses a half-skipped revision
description:
SPIDR prerequisite of task-de0598236f3b4d95aa3b6098b9d56995 (architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05), cut on the DATA axis. That row measured at ~10 distinct files with two of them already at or over the per-file cap; this row carries the one piece that had no home at all.

HUMAN DECISION, 2026-09-05, taken in the REPL after the architect measured that the toggle had no precedent (`git grep -ln 'skipDesign|GoalSettings|perGoal' -- apps/daemon/src` = ZERO hits) and that its obvious home was closed: `goal.create`'s payload is exact-arity `["instructions","title"]` (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:295), so widening it is a separate multi-file roster job on the critical path. The human chose: RECORD THE SKIP ON THE EXISTING DESIGN AGGREGATE. No new command kind, no new aggregate, no vocabulary or registry backfill. The alternatives considered and rejected were widening `goal.create` (roster job) and a project-level flag (would have forced DoD-6 of the parent to be rewritten from "per-goal" to "per-project").

OBJECTIVE: make "this goal plans without a design" a durable, readable fact on `design:<goalId>`.

DELIVERABLE WHEN DONE: a design revision can carry a SKIPPED marker; `designRead` answers it; and a revision that is half-skipped - marked skipped while still carrying sections, or marked un-skipped while carrying none - is REFUSED with a stable code and its layer.

MEASURED AT HEAD f3b94eaa (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-b63fabf3:
- `apps/daemon/src/design/` holds 9 files landed by task-5e90317e (DONE, sha 34baaf52, reviewed: 48 tests, three drills). This row extends that contract; it does not rewrite it.
- `design-contracts.ts:39` `DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS` = `["apiSurface","componentList","dataModel","nonFunctional","openDecisions","screens"]` - SIX keys, `/** Sorted, and compared by exact arity. */`.
- `design-contracts.ts:44` `DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS` = the FIVE sections, `/** named apart from openDecisions so a dropped one names itself */`.
- `exactDesignRecord` at :150 and `decodeDesignRevision` at :232 are the arity gate. `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS` at :65 is the closed code->layer map; `designRefusal` at :120 takes the CODE only and reads the layer from that map, so a call site structurally cannot mint a disagreeing pair. Use it; never pass a layer literal.
- THE BLAST RADIUS IS CONTAINED AND MEASURED: `git grep -ln 'DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS|DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS|openDecisions' -- . ':!.moe'` returns exactly FOUR files, all under apps/daemon/src/design/ - design-contracts.ts, design-contracts.test.ts, design-store.test.ts, design-test-fixtures.ts. Nothing outside that directory names the revision keys.
- `design-records.ts:31` `DESIGN_RECORD_KEYS` does NOT mirror the revision keys (`revision` is one key), so the RECORD shape is untouched by this row.
- `design.submit` / `design.read` are NOT yet published on any command roster (`git grep -n 'design\.submit|design\.read'` hits only design-store.ts:155, a record field). That publication is task-06ac0da1's and this row does NOT need it: this row changes a decoder and its aggregate, not a wire.

THE HAZARD THAT DEFINES THIS ROW: `DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS` is compared by EXACT ARITY. Adding a seventh key makes every existing six-key revision payload REFUSE - every fixture, every test arm, every future caller. That is not a side effect to absorb quietly; it is the main event. Either the new key is genuinely required on every revision (and all four files move together in one commit), or the decode admits both arities deliberately and a test pins WHICH. Decide it at plan time, say which in the completion record, and drill it: a six-key revision must still round-trip, or must refuse with a named code - never silently.

NOT IN SCOPE - owned by named rows:
- The affordance surface reading this marker to skip the step - the successor row filed alongside this one.
- The wrapper staffing a design seat, and any mission text - task-de0598236f3b4d95aa3b6098b9d56995.
- Publishing `design.submit`/`design.read` on the command roster or over MCP - task-06ac0da1 and task-7f9f20c7.
- Any UI - task-8a6d6660's child 3.

Also run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck` and quote their count lines.
definitionOfDone: A design revision can be marked SKIPPED on the `design:<goalId>` aggregate, and `designRead` answers that marker distinguishably from both "no design has ever been submitted" and "a real design exists". Assert all THREE states against a real store built by the production journey (the pattern task-5e90317e used), not against a hand-built fixture object - a two-state assertion cannot tell a skip from an absent read, which is the exact confusion this row exists to remove.

The arity decision is MADE, PINNED and DRILLED. `DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS` is compared by exact arity (design-contracts.ts:39 comment, enforced at `exactDesignRecord`:150), so a seventh key changes what every existing payload decodes to. State in the completion record which rule you chose - required-on-every-revision, or both arities admitted - and pin it with a test that asserts a SIX-key revision's outcome by name (round-trips, or refuses with a specific code). `expect(result.ok).toBe(false)` alone does not satisfy this clause.

A HALF-SKIPPED revision is refused with a stable code AND its layer asserted: marked skipped while still carrying sections, and marked un-skipped while carrying no sections. The code comes through `designRefusal(<code>)` so the layer is read from `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS` (design-contracts.ts:65) - a layer string literal at any throw site is a defect, because `designRefusal` accepts no layer argument precisely so no call site can mint a disagreeing pair. If a NEW code is added, it joins that closed map and `DESIGN_CODES` derives from the map's keys, never from a second hand-written list.

All four measured consumers move in the SAME commit and none is left decoding the old arity: apps/daemon/src/design/design-contracts.ts, design-contracts.test.ts, design-store.test.ts, design-test-fixtures.ts. Re-run `git grep -ln 'DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS|DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS|openDecisions' -- . ':!.moe'` at the delivered tree and confirm it still returns exactly those four - a fifth consumer appearing mid-flight is a stop-and-report, not an extra path to take.

MUTATION DRILL, quoted with its failing line, restored and proved: flip the skipped/sections consistency check so a half-skipped revision is admitted, and confirm the arm from DoD-3 goes RED naming the code (not merely "threw"). `git status --porcelain` the mutated paths FIRST; every file here is TRACKED so an empty `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof, in a call SEPARATE from the restore - say so explicitly rather than leaving global rail 13 unaddressed.

Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence here and must not be quoted as such - vitest.config.ts:32 includes no `apps/**`, so it runs zero tests against this row's files. Attribute any foreign red by the merge-base/HEAD failing-path delta intersected with apps/daemon/src/design/.
taskRails: DATA SHAPE ONLY, INSIDE apps/daemon/src/design/. This row publishes no command kind, offers no affordance step, staffs no seat and writes no mission text. If a step needs the surface or the wrapper to be meaningful, it belongs to a successor row - say so and move on.

EXACT ARITY IS THE POINT, NOT AN OBSTACLE. `DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS` is compared by arity, so a seventh key redefines every existing payload's outcome. Do not work around it by loosening `exactDesignRecord` for everything - that would silently admit unknown keys on every design and delete the guarantee task-5e90317e shipped.

REFUSALS COME THROUGH `designRefusal(<code>)`, which reads the layer from the closed `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS` map and accepts no layer argument. A layer string literal at a throw site is a defect even when it happens to be the right string.

This row EXTENDS a DONE row's contract (task-5e90317e, sha 34baaf52). Read its reviewSummary before editing: three drills and 48 tests already guard this directory. Do not delete or weaken an existing arm to make a new one fit.

implementationPlan.description: THE SKIP SHAPE AND THE DISCRIMINATED DECODE. apps/daemon/src/design/design-contracts.ts only (259 lines - target <=250, hard cap 400; keep the addition tight). THE ARCHITECTURAL DECISION IS MADE HERE, NOT LEFT TO YOU - DoD-2 asks which arity rule was chosen, and the answer is TWO ADMITTED ARITIES, DISCRIMINATED ON THE PRESENCE OF `skipped`. Reasoning to carry into the completion record: adding `skipped` as a seventh REQUIRED key would make every existing six-key payload refuse, force every real design submission to carry `skipped: false` as wire noise, and break both fixtures and every arm task-5e90317e shipped. A separate skip shape breaks nothing and makes the half-skipped refusal fall out of exact arity instead of needing a bespoke consistency check. (1) Add `export const DESIGN_SKIP_KEYS = Object.freeze(["reason", "skipped"] as const)` - SORTED, like every roster in this file - and `export interface DesignSkip { readonly reason: string; readonly skipped: true }`. `reason` is bounded text via the existing `boundedDesignText`:144 (a skip is a product decision; an unexplained one is a decision nobody can review later). `skipped` must be the LITERAL `true`: a non-skip is expressed by submitting an actual design, never by `skipped: false`. (2) Widen the result type: `export type DesignRevisionOrSkip = DesignRevision | DesignSkip` and change `DesignRevisionResult`:117 to carry it. Add a type guard `export function isDesignSkip(value: DesignRevisionOrSkip): value is DesignSkip` - consumers (the surface row task-217f40b7, the mission row task-de059823) will narrow with it, so it must be exported, not inlined. (3) In `decodeDesignRevision`:232, discriminate BEFORE the existing arity check: if `Reflect.ownKeys(value)` contains "skipped", decode via `exactDesignRecord(value, DESIGN_SKIP_KEYS)` and require `skipped === true` plus `boundedDesignText(reason)`; otherwise fall through to the existing six-key path UNCHANGED. Do not touch the existing path's logic - it is guarded by 48 tests. (4) ADD NO NEW REFUSAL CODE. `DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID` @ REQUEST already means "the exact-key roster refused the submitted revision" and covers every malformed case here. A new code would mean a new entry in the closed `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS` map and a boundary-roster backfill for no gain - say in the record that you deliberately reused it.

THE SKIP SHAPE AND THE DISCRIMINATED DECODE — apps/daemon/src/design/design-contracts.ts ONLY. 259 -> 313 lines (target 250 was already exceeded before this row; hard cap 400 respected, no reformatting, no existing line touched except the one type annotation named below).

ARITY RULE IMPLEMENTED AS PLANNED: TWO ADMITTED ARITIES, discriminated on an OWN `skipped` marker. Four additions, one annotation change, zero deletions.

(1) `DESIGN_SKIP_KEYS = Object.freeze(["reason", "skipped"] as const)` — SORTED like every roster in the file, placed directly after DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS. Its doc records WHY it is arity-compared: `{skipped, reason, ...six sections}` is eight keys and satisfies NEITHER roster, so the half-skipped refusal falls out of exact arity instead of needing a bespoke consistency check that a later refactor could quietly drop.

(2) `interface DesignSkip { readonly reason: string; readonly skipped: true }` — `skipped` is the LITERAL `true`, not `boolean`. TypeScript therefore makes `skipped: false` unrepresentable at the type level, and `decodeSkip` refuses it at runtime, so the invariant is enforced twice by different mechanisms.

(3) `export type DesignRevisionOrSkip = DesignRevision | DesignSkip` and `export function isDesignSkip(value: DesignRevisionOrSkip): value is DesignSkip` — EXPORTED, not inlined, because two consumer rows narrow with it (task-217f40b7 the affordance surface, task-de059823 the compiler mission); an inlined check would be re-implemented per consumer and drift. Implemented with `Object.hasOwn(value, "skipped")` (lib ES2024 per tsconfig.base.json, and `Object.hasOwn` is already used across apps/control-room), so the guard is own-property-only for the same reason the discriminator is.

(4) `DesignRevisionResult`'s success member widened from `DesignRevision` to `DesignRevisionOrSkip`. THIS IS THE ONLY EXISTING LINE CHANGED IN THE FILE.

(5) `decodeDesignRevision` — the discrimination is the FIRST statement, before the six-key arity gate, and the existing six-key path is byte-for-byte untouched below it. Two new private helpers:
  - `carriesSkipMarker(value)`: `typeof value === "object" && value !== null && Reflect.ownKeys(value).includes("skipped")`. `Reflect.ownKeys`, NOT `in` — `"skipped" in value` walks the prototype chain and would re-open precisely the inherited-member hole `exactDesignRecord` closes; the null/typeof guard is required because `Reflect.ownKeys(null)` throws a TypeError rather than answering false.
  - `decodeSkip(value)`: `exactDesignRecord(value, DESIGN_SKIP_KEYS)` then `item["skipped"] !== true` then `!boundedDesignText(item["reason"])` — any one of the three refuses. Returns a FRESH frozen `{reason, skipped: true}` built in roster order, matching the existing path's copy-into-a-fresh-frozen-record discipline so a caller retaining the input cannot mutate what the daemon persisted, and so two encodes of one skip are byte-identical.

(6) NO NEW REFUSAL CODE — deliberate. Every refusal above is `designRefusal("DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID")`, whose own doc at DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS:65 already reads "The exact-key section roster refused the submitted revision". `designRefusal` takes the CODE only and reads REQUEST out of the closed map, so no call site here can mint a disagreeing pair and no layer string literal appears anywhere in the diff. A new code would mean a new entry in that closed map plus a boundary-roster backfill for zero diagnostic gain.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN DESCRIPTION, both made before planning. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. The plan (5 steps, 6 files) is built on the corrected facts; where description and plan disagree, THE PLAN IS AUTHORITY.

## 1. The description says "exactly FOUR files". It is FIVE, maybe six.

I filed it after running `git grep -ln 'DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS|DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS|openDecisions'` — a grep of the KEY ROSTERS, not of the TYPE. `git grep -n 'DesignRevision\b'` additionally names:

    apps/daemon/src/design/design-records.ts:11   import { type DesignRevision }
    apps/daemon/src/design/design-records.ts:45   readonly revision: DesignRevision;

Measured union, all under `apps/daemon/src/design/`: design-contracts.ts, design-records.ts, design-contracts.test.ts, design-store.test.ts, design-test-fixtures.ts. design-store.ts is a maybe-sixth — `readDesignRevision`:189 returns `DesignReadResult` so the widened type should flow, and the plan tells the worker to settle that by typecheck rather than by editing it speculatively.

This is global rail 18 in miniature — grep the SHAPE, not the symbol — and it is recorded rather than quietly fixed so the next census does both greps. A file outside `apps/daemon/src/design/` remains a stop-and-report.

## 2. The description implies a seventh key. The plan chooses TWO ARITIES instead.

The description's hazard paragraph frames the choice as "either the new key is required on every revision, or the decode admits both arities" and leaves it open. Leaving the one architectural question in the row to the worker was my error; DoD-2 asks them to *state* the rule, not to *pick* it. **The rule is: two admitted arities, discriminated on the presence of `skipped`.**

    DESIGN_SKIP_KEYS = ["reason", "skipped"]        // skipped is the LITERAL true
    DesignRevisionOrSkip = DesignRevision | DesignSkip
    decodeDesignRevision: Reflect.ownKeys has "skipped"
                            ? exact arity over DESIGN_SKIP_KEYS
                            : the existing six-key path, UNCHANGED

Why, so it is not re-litigated: a seventh required key would make every existing six-key payload refuse (both fixtures plus every arm task-5e90317e shipped), force every REAL design submission to carry `skipped: false` as permanent wire noise, and make the design seat's brief teach a model to declare it is *not* skipping. Two arities break nothing, and the half-skipped refusal then falls out of exact arity rather than needing a bespoke consistency check — `{skipped:true, reason, ...six sections}` is 8 keys and fails both rosters.

`skipped` is the literal `true`, not a boolean: `skipped: false` would otherwise be a lawful revision carrying no design at all, which is the exact state DoD-3 requires be refused. A non-skip is expressed by submitting a design.

**No new refusal code.** `DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID` @ REQUEST already reads "the exact-key section roster refused the submitted revision" and covers every case here. A new code means a new entry in the closed `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS` map plus a boundary-roster backfill, for no diagnostic gain.

## One thing the composition gives free, and the plan pins it

`submitDesignRevision` (design-store.ts:130) decodes FIRST and calls `readApprovedDesignContract` SECOND — so a SKIP is subject to the same Gate-1-approved fence as a real design. You cannot skip the design for a goal whose contract was never approved, which is exactly the window task-217f40b7's surface offers the step in. Step 4 asserts it (`DESIGN_CONTRACT_NOT_APPROVED` @ `CONTRACT_AUTHORITY`) so a later refactor cannot quietly drop it.

`isDesignSkip` is EXPORTED on purpose: task-217f40b7 (surface) and task-de059823 (compiler mission) both narrow with it. Inlining the check would have each consumer re-implement the discriminator and drift.

THE ARITY DECISION IS MADE AT PLAN TIME, not delegated. DoD-2 asks the worker to state which rule was chosen; leaving the CHOICE to them would have been an architect declining the one architectural question in the row.

CHOSEN - TWO ADMITTED ARITIES, discriminated on the presence of `skipped`. A skip is a 2-key record {reason, skipped:true}; a design is the existing 6-key record. `decodeDesignRevision` discriminates before its arity check and the existing six-key path is untouched.

The half-skipped refusal would then need a bespoke consistency check instead of falling out of arity.
REJECTED - a separate SKIP EVENT TYPE on the same aggregate. Cleaner in the abstract, but a new event type needs a writer, and a writer needs a command kind - the measured three-row job (mem:decision-a-new-command-kind-is-a-three-row-job). The human's decision was explicitly to avoid a roster job.
REJECTED - a new refusal code such as DESIGN_SKIP_INVALID. `DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID` @ REQUEST is already documented as "the exact-key section roster refused the submitted revision" and covers every case here. REJECTED - a bare {skipped: true} with no reason. A skip is a product decision; an unexplained one is unreviewable later, and `boundedDesignText` already exists to bound it at no cost.

planningNotes.risks:
FIRST - THE SIX-KEY PATH MUST BE PROVABLY UNCHANGED. The entire justification for two arities is that nothing existing breaks. If a fixture or an existing arm needs editing to stay green, the discrimination is in the wrong place - fix the decode, do not edit task-5e90317e's arms. Its 48 tests and three drills are not this row's to re-grade, and weakening one to fit is a reject.

SECOND - THE DISCRIMINATOR IS A PROTOTYPE HOLE IF WRITTEN WITH `in`. `exactDesignRecord` deliberately rejects inherited members and non-Object prototypes; a discriminator using `"skipped" in value` inherits from the prototype chain and re-opens exactly that. Use `Reflect.ownKeys`.

THIRD - `skipped` MUST BE THE LITERAL `true`. A boolean admits `skipped: false`, which is then a lawful revision carrying no design - the half-skipped state DoD-3 exists to refuse.

FOURTH - the row DESCRIPTION says four files and the measured union is five (six if design-store.ts needs an annotation). Trust the greps, not the prose, and say so in the record. A sixth file OUTSIDE apps/daemon/src/design/ is a stop-and-report.

FIFTH - do not add a refusal code. A new code means a new entry in the closed DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS map and a boundary-roster backfill (mem:new-layer-constant-must-reuse-a-rostered-layer), for no diagnostic gain over DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID.

SIXTH - design-contracts.ts is 259 lines, already past the 250 target. Keep the skip shape, the guard and the discrimination tight; do not reformat the file.

SEVENTH - the skip must survive the DURABLE round trip, not only the request decode. `decodeDesignRevisionBytes`:254 maps any decode failure to DESIGN_RECORD_MALFORMED, so a skip that decodes on submit but not on read would be stored and then unreadable - a silent one-way door. Assert the read side.

EIGHTH - CONSUMERS ARE WAITING ON THE EXPORTED SHAPE. task-217f40b7 (surface) and task-de059823 (compiler mission) both narrow with `isDesignSkip`. Export it; do not inline the check, or each consumer re-implements the discriminator and they drift.

NINTH - shared checkout. Peer dirt under .moe/ and .grok/ is NEVER a stop condition: note it, never revert, stash or `git add -A`. Report every path you touch in complete_step.modifiedFiles.

completionSummary:
A design revision can now be SKIPPED on design:<goalId>; designRead answers it; a half-skipped revision is refused with a stable code and its layer.

ARITY RULE CHOSEN: TWO ADMITTED ARITIES, discriminated on the presence of an OWN `skipped` marker. A skip is the 2-key {reason, skipped:true}; the design stays the unchanged 6-key record. A seventh REQUIRED key was rejected because it would make every existing 6-key payload refuse, force every real design to carry `skipped:false` as wire noise, and break task-5e90317e's fixtures and arms. THE SIX-KEY PATH IS PROVABLY UNCHANGED — its logic was not touched, and the arm "admits the complete revision and returns every section" (design-contracts.test.ts:89) asserts the six-key outcome BY NAME: it round-trips, `isDesignSkip` narrows it FALSE, and every section compares by value. That narrowing assertion is load-bearing, not decoration: without it a skip returned on that path would compare six undefineds against six undefineds and pass.

NO NEW REFUSAL CODE. `DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID` @ REQUEST was reused deliberately — it already means "the exact-key roster refused the submitted revision". A new code would mean a new entry in the closed DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS map plus a boundary-roster backfill for zero diagnostic gain. Every refusal goes through `designRefusal(<code>)`, code only; layer literals appear ONLY in the closed roster and map, ZERO at any throw site.

THE HALF-SKIPPED REFUSAL FALLS OUT OF EXACT ARITY rather than a bespoke check: `decodeSkip` re-applies `exactDesignRecord(value, DESIGN_SKIP_KEYS)`, so skipped-with-sections (8 keys) and bare {skipped:true} (1 key) both fail the roster; `skipped:false` fails the literal-`true` guard. Discriminator uses `Reflect.ownKeys`, and `isDesignSkip` uses `Object.hasOwn` + `=== true`, so neither re-opens the prototype hole exactDesignRecord closes.
